summary: Pierce County, WA: a 70-ft timber lookout built in 1937, used by the AWS in 1942, and removed in 1969. The site is on Hancock timberland that requires a permit.

facts.design: 70-foot timber tower with L-6 cab and ground cabin living quarters
facts.status_note: Tower removed in 1969; no source we read describes remains on the ground

access.note: Land is part of Hancock Timber's Eatonville Forest; WillhiteWeb says a permit is required

visit.trail_note: About 5 miles on roads from Eatonville to a gate; per WillhiteWeb a permit is required

events.note: 70-foot timber tower with L-6 cab; phone lines placed the same year
Used by the AWS, activated March 9, 1942
Structure lasted until 1969 and was removed

evidence.supports: built 1937, 70-foot timber tower with L-6 cab and ground cabin, removed 1969
evidence.quote: Built in 1937, this 70' timber tower with L-6 cab and accompanying ground cabin living quarters were removed in 1969.

evidence.supports: built in 1937 with phone lines placed
evidence.quote: The Ohop Lookout was built and phone lines placed in 1937.

evidence.supports: 70-foot timber tower with L-6 cab and ground cabin
evidence.quote: It was a 70 foot timber tower with an L-6 cab and accompanying ground cabin living quarters.

evidence.supports: used by the AWS, activated March 9, 1942
evidence.quote: The location was used by the AWS, activated March 9, 1942.

evidence.supports: lookout continued for fire; structure lasted until 1969
evidence.quote: The lookout continued for fire after and the structure lasted until 1969.

evidence.supports: site known as the Ohop Benchmark
evidence.quote: The Ohop Benchmark was once the site of a lookout tower.

evidence.supports: 2003 views after a timber harvest; trees have grown back
evidence.quote: In 2003, I had excellent views after a timber harvest but trees have now grown back now.
The tree farm was purchased by Hancock Timber and it is now in their Eatonville Forest, where a permit is required.
From Eatonville, go east from the town 4 way stop.

notes_for_editor: Brief record checks out: coordinates, 711.7 m elevation and US 1292 / WA 192 match the cached pages. No corrections. Built, AWS use and 1969 removal agree across the three sites. The permit rule and the 2003 visit come from one undated WillhiteWeb page, so check Hancock Timber's current access rules before anyone publishes a visit route.
